leads.question: In the shipped monad 0.16.7 validator binary, does each literal-folding arm of the emitter (Emitter::modop_optimized, div_optimized, mod_optimized, shift_by_literal, and the literal arms of signextend and byte) compute the specified word for the literal operands that occur in the deployed PoolManager? List those literals from out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt of cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work (the literal power-of-two moduli are the PUSH13 2^96 at pc 22639 and the PUSH17 2^128 at pc 22378; at pc 20958, 22763 and 22721 the literal 2^96 is the second operand and takes the general runtime mulmod; the literal modulus 1,000,000 at pc 22513 and the all-ones moduli do not have a single set bit), lift the gcc code of each arm from the package text into the cycle 27 x86 model of theme-monad-package-read, and run it on those literals with the 2,004,096 operand set of the countl_zero check.
leads.why: Monad validators run the PoolManager as native code built by these gcc routines, while every eth_call and every harness run so far used the interpreter or a clang build. A wrong fold on a literal the PoolManager carries would change FullMath.mulDiv results, and with them swap amounts and fee growth, in mined blocks only, and an ordinary swap reaches it.

leads.question: Were the native blocks for src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 (overflow fallback), SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 (amount above 2^160), and Position.sol:94-96 (512 bit branch of the Q128 mulDiv) entered by any case of the repaired harness at v0.16.7? Map those source lines to PoolManager block offsets with opcodes/jumpmap.json, look them up in the per-case coverage of cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/out/c25-all-cov and c26-all-cov and in the 530 cases of theme-never-run-math-sides, and for every block not entered build a case with the cycle 25 driver that enters it and compare interpreter, native code and pyevm.py words.
leads.why: F-130 shows these branches have never run in a mined Monad block and that no RPC call can run them natively. If native code computed one of them wrongly, the first ordinary large swap or fee collection that takes the branch would pay the wrong amount from pool funds on every validator.

leads.question: Do the 37 PoolManager blocks whose emitted code changed between Monad v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 and that no harness case entered (cov-changed.json in cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/out, among them 0x40d7 with a literal shifted by a computed count, 0xed4, 0x3aae and 0x593c with word-wise loads, and 0x2f7b to 0x2fe7) give the interpreter's result when driven by cases built to reach them? Name the source line of each block first and drop those that only build revert data.
leads.why: These blocks run new emitter code on mainnet validators since 0.16.7 and have no test at all. A block on a math or settlement path that computes a different word in native code would let an ordinary call change pool accounting in mined blocks.

leads.question: Without running it, does the aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu tempo v1.19.1 release binary compute the specified results in its jump destination kernel and in ruint 1.21.1 mul_mod, div_rem and the shifts? leads.question: Which clearance of a stale sync (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364) rests on the claim that a router always calls sync again before it pays? List every shared-transaction context where a second party's frame follows an ordinary attacker's frame in the same transaction (ERC-4337 bundles on World Chain and the other chains with an EntryPoint, Tempo type 0x76 batches with a fee payer, Base Everest phases, Multicall3 relayers), and for the deployed Universal Router and PositionManager on each network read whether any settle path reads balanceOf without its own sync first.
leads.why: A stale synced currency left by an attacker is credited to whoever settles next. The clearances so far checked the core and the transaction boundary, and periphery behaviour was assumed. If a widely used router settles without its own sync, the attacker's earlier sync would shift credit between ordinary users in one bundle.
